text:
eli: Heads-up from today's onboarding run: sampleapp + batching helper produced wrong embedding->query pairing after an SDK retry. Scores were assigned to the wrong ids and some vectors had missing padding.

zoe: Oof. Which helpers/SDKs and a tiny repro would help.

eli: Repro: sampleapp uses the official batch helper which packets items into chunks and sends. Trigger: token refresh mid-batch then a transient 502 on the first chunk. Helper retries the chunk and reassembles multiple pieces. We log the original send as:```
[docA{id:A,vec:[0.01,0.02,0.03]}, docB{id:B,vec:[0.1,0.2,0.3]}, docC{id:C,vec:[0.9,0.8,0.7]}]
```But after retry the reassembled payload sometimes looks like B,A,C and docB's vector lost trailing zeros (padding dropped). Server returns scores in positional order so mapping by index flips results.

mohit: Interesting. Is this Node-only?

eli: Node shows it consistently when the helper uses an ArrayBuffer-concat optimization. Rust sampleapp (community contrib) had a different serializer path and returned a nested response shape when retry happened. Go returned a flat shape. So three variants in the wild which makes consumers brittle.

zoe: Sounds like two failure classes: (1) nondeterministic reassembly ordering when retries merge chunks, and (2) serializer parity diverging between retry paths (flat vs nested response JSON). Both break index-based mapping.

mohit: Short-term mitigation: always include a stable id per item (we do), and map response values by id instead of by index. Also validate vector length on receive and fail loudly if dim != expected. Example mapping shim:```
function normalize(resp, ids){
  const scores = resp.scores || (resp.results && resp.results.scores) || [];
  return ids.reduce((m,id,i)=> (m[id]=scores[i] ?? null, m), {});
}
```This still assumes positions align but helps until we get server echo.

eli: For the immediate sampleapp fix I added a second guard: require the server to echo per-item id in the response; if missing, client rejects the batch and logs for DE-12001. That made the onboarding crash obvious instead of silently misranking.

zoe: Filed DE-12001: "batch helper retry reassembly + serializer parity" and assigned to eng-runtime + sdk-maintainers. Tasks: add per-item `_seq` on send, never mutate original arrays during reassemble, and server should echo per-item id in all paths (including partial success). Also add serializer parity tests across Node/Rust/Go simulating token refresh + transient 502 + randomized reassembly order.

infra-bot: DE-12001 created and linked to #eng-runtime and #sdk-maintainers.

mohit: Extra note: we found one remote cause where a mid-batch auth refresh triggered an alternate code-path that stripped batch headers; that caused the server to treat two halves separately and return different JSON shapes. Fix: helper should pause batching during auth refresh or carry headers forward on retry.

eli: I also propose a helper lint rule: warn if mixed vector lengths are batched without explicit padding or declared `dim`. That would have caught the missing padding issue quickly.

zoe: Agreed. Add integration test to CI that simulates auth refresh mid-batch + 502 + retry and asserts final assembled order equals original using `_seq` and that server echoes ids.

eli: For anyone blocked now: (1) map by id on response, (2) validate dims before computing similarities, (3) avoid assuming positional alignment when retries are enabled. I'll push a tiny sampleapp patch and doc blurb with those three lines.

devex-bot: Noted in onboarding checklist: "always include stable per-item ids, validate dims, and don't rely on index alignment when retries enabled".

zoe: Thanks all — closing this thread for the onboarding run. Follow DE-12001 for runtime/SDK parity fixes. :thumbsup:
